executivePulse.interpretation: Daily Check 2026-08-10: Since the previous Daily Snapshot, no new signal has been identified that robustly exceeds the TAIL admission threshold. Existing theses and scores remain unchanged until new evidence clears the Admission Gates.

signals.title: Server DRAM shortage deepens towards 2027
signals.summary: AI servers, higher memory per system and constrained wafer allocation increase the risk of a structural server DRAM undersupply in 2027.
signals.analysis: Secure procurement earlier; spot availability loses importance relative to multi-year LTAs and strategic allocation.

signals.title: SK hynix flags potential demand overhang beyond 2030
signals.summary: Capacity expansion may not keep pace long term with AI-driven demand and rising memory content per system.
signals.analysis: The traditional short memory cycle is being overshadowed by structural capacity lock-in.

signals.title: Hyperscalers lock memory and flash via multi-year LTAs
signals.summary: Multi-year offtake agreements bind capacity and increasingly divide the market into strategically supplied and unprotected buyers.
signals.analysis: LTAs become a competitive advantage. Distributors must sell availability, not just price.
